messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT (2965439999) - dedicated-pool 'cardioai-prod-vpc' reporting GPU capacity exhaustion. Tenant: CardioAI (enterprise/VPC). New rejections: 15% 503s on /v1/stream for model 'cardioai/opt-13b', queue depth spiking. Runbook pointer: <runbooks/dedicated-vpc-exhaustion>. Pager: @priya oncall.

priya: I'm on it. Pulling pool telemetry and recent autoscaler activity. First glance: heavy inference from scheduled training-validation job from CardioAI's internal pipeline at 04:10 UTC. Pool is single-tenant in a VPC (no cross-tenant migration available).

emma: autoscaler log shows scale attempt at 04:12 -> provisioning blocked by org policy: `vpc-dedicated-burst-requires-approval`. Cloud API returned success for instance reservation but security lock prevented attachment.

priya: can you paste snippet?

emma: ```
2026-03-15T04:12:07Z autoscaler | requested +6 gpus
2026-03-15T04:12:09Z cloudsec  | policy: vpc-dedicated-burst -> approval_required
2026-03-15T04:12:09Z autoscaler | aborting scale-up, awaiting manual approval
```

zeke: paging sec-approvals now. ops-approvals-bot, trigger emergency approval flow for CardioAI? Need rapid attach, same-region, same-account only.

ops-approvals-bot: Approval request submitted: request-id req-CA-20260315-11. Notifying: infra-security, compliance, finance. Expected manual review time 10-20m.

csn-ana: CSM ping: CardioAI says this is their nightly validation job; they can suspend it for up to 45m if we request, but they require explicit confirmation we will not change their model config or route data off-VPC.

priya: good to know. Temporary hosted fallback is not allowed by their contract. So options are limited: (1) get security approval to attach additional GPUs in the VPC (fast if approved), (2) ask CardioAI to pause their batch job (they said they can), (3) lifecycle-level throttle: kill or throttle long-running validation workers inside the pool, (4) spin up temporary spot GPU nodes in same VPC account (requires approval as well). We should coordinate two parallel tracks: ask CardioAI to pause, and request approval.

leo: I can attempt a targeted throttle first: identify validation job pods with label `cardioai.validation/nightly` and scale them down. Command: 
```
kubectl -n pools-cardioai get pods -l job=cardioai.validation/nightly -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}\n'
```
Will run a drain that keeps X workers alive to avoid cold-start regressions.

priya: do it, but mention in channel before you scale anything. We need the CSM consent if we will affect their job more than transiently.

csn-ana: CardioAI SRE (via DM) says pause is approved for 30m. Proceed with throttling if that speeds recovery.

leo: scaling validation job from 12 -> 2 replicas (keeping metrics exporter alive). Command executed. Job pods terminating gracefully.

incident-bot: Autoscaler retry attempt queued after approval. Current pool utilization dropping from 98% -> 72% in 4m. 503 rate down to 6%.

priya: thanks. Still seeing some long-tail latency for small percentage of real-time traffic. Since we can't route to hosted, we should enable short-term request queuing with client-visible Retry-After header for heavy requests. Ops: set soft-throttle at 200 concurrent requests per GPU for next 20m.

emma: applied soft-throttle config: `runtime.set_throttle --pool cardioai-prod-vpc --concurrency 200 --window 20m`. Routing proxy will return 429 + Retry-After when threshold exceeded. Logs show 18 requests with Retry-After in last 2m. 503s steady at 1.2%.

zeke: update on approval: infra-security reviewing req-CA-20260315-11, security asks for an attestation from customer that no exfiltration will be required and that adding nodes will be within same subnet. CSM Ana can obtain immediately.

csn-ana: I have CardioAI attestation in hand. Uploaded to approval request. Please expedite.

ops-approvals-bot: Approval granted by infra-security and compliance. Request-id req-CA-20260315-11 -> status: APPROVED. Auto-attach permitted for up to +4 GPUs for 2 hours.

priya: initiating attach now: `rictl allocate-vpc-gpus --pool cardioai-prod-vpc --gpus 4 --ttl 2h --request-id req-CA-20260315-11`.

emma: allocation returned success. New nodes attached and registered to pool. Telemetry shows queue drained, 503 back to baseline (<0.2%).

priya: mitigation summary for handoff: throttled validation job (leo), applied soft-throttle runtime config (emma), obtained security/compliance approval and attached +4 GPUs under emergency approval (priya/emma/ops-approvals-bot), customer paused extra load for 30m (csn-ana). Current status: mitigated -> monitoring.

priya: immediate follow-ups assigned: - leo: confirm there is no residual preemption for CardioAI workloads and monitor pod restarts (owner: leo) - emma: schedule autoscaler rule change to surface `vpc-dedicated-burst-requires-approval` earlier as an alert (owner: emma) - zeke: draft emergency runbook addendum for VPC-dedicated single-tenant pools (owner: zeke) - natalie (capacity team): evaluate reserved burst allowance for CardioAI to avoid manual approvals (owner: natalie)

priya: handing off to @leo for monitoring and closure. I'll open incident doc and tag compliance/security approvals. Incident link: <incidents/2965439999>.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: INCIDENT (2965439999) status -> mitigated; assigned to leo for monitoring and postmortem.

leo: taking. I'll watch for 30m of stable windows (5m buckets) and then close. If any regressions, escalate to infra pager. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
